full_judgment: It is obvious from this observation that the intention of delaying or defeating the decree was presumed by their Lordships in this decision from the facts and circumstances of that particular case. We do not think that this observation is made in absolute terms to be applied to each case, and it does not require the authority of any decision to hold that intention being in abstract, has to be gathered from the attending facts and circumstances of each case. The conclusion arrived at in this observation by their Lordships shall be applicable to the facts and circumstances of that case, records of which were before their Lordships and the presumptions that were drawn by their Lordships from those facts are but for that case. In the instant case we have already set out the allegation s made in paragraph 5 of the plaint and paragraph 2 of the application, a positive statement was made that the mother ship registered in a Latin American country having discharged the cargo left the jurisdiction of Chittagong court for a foreign destination and defendant No. 2 the agent of .defendant No. 1 has no property to satisfy the decree, if any, passed by the court. In these circumstances, the inevitable presumption from the departure of the mother ship and the failure of defendant No. 2, the agent or defendant No. 1 the carrier, to set out a list of properties owed by defendant No. 2 is that the intention was but to delay or defeat the execution of any future decree passed in favour of the plaintiff. It may also be mentioned that in the normal course of business a foreign ship does not call on a foreign port unless it is chartered for the purpose.
